summary: Instrumented the path that previously aborted the sweep so a mis-ordered configuration change becomes data rather than a crash. The per-step apply now runs each committed EntryConfChangeV2 under a recover and counts a rejection in a new invalid_change_applies counter reported by invariant_sweep_summary. That is the prerequisite for re-enabling configuration events aimed at an existing serving voter - the last item the open gap names - because a lag-driven mis-ordering would then show up as a number instead of killing the run, and a zero would say the propose-time guard kept such changes out. The draft-side run reproduces the executed counters exactly and adds invalid_change_applies=0 (elections=470, ordinary proposals=461, conf_change_proposals=262, restarts=429, unapplied_conf_change_states=48, stalled_states=0, violations=0), consistent with the alreadyPending/alreadyJoint rewrite recorded as knowledge last turn; because that is construction feedback only, the submission requests isolated execution of these bytes so the zero is receipt-backed before it is relied on. The event set is otherwise the executed revision (four real state machines with node 4 starting outside the configuration, single-change proposals half of them JointImplicit, application lag skipping one node's apply about one time in six, restarts rebuilt from persisted hard state and applied ConfState, and the liveness witness with its antecedent counter), and the request states plainly that the counter's cause is not claimed - only the occurrence of a change a node's own tracker rejected - and that the demotion variant is not yet enabled.
